narrative:
The model predicts a 90% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you received other job offers while working here, and how long you have been with this current organization. 

Your total professional experience of 6-10 years was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, half have only 1-5 years of experience, so your longer background appears to make you more marketable and mobile. The fact that you have received other job opportunities was the second biggest factor, also pulling the prediction toward departure; most employees the model predicts will stay never receive such offers. Finally, your 1-5 years in this specific role also contributed toward predicting you will leave, as shorter tenure in the current organization often signals less attachment.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture of someone who is experienced, visible to other employers, and not deeply rooted here yet.

The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths, better rewards, or addressing your work-life balance challenges. You may want to reflect on what would make you want to stay long-term.
